paper.title: Mixture Martingales Revisited with Applications to Sequential Tests and Confidence Intervals

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential identification problem (partition identification) in exponential family bandit models
unmapped: fixed-confidence identification of which cell of a known partition O_1..O_M of open sets contains the mean vector (M hypotheses); the learner knows the partition
settings.definition_quote: we consider $M$ hypotheses $\cH_1 = (\bm \mu \in \cO_1), \dots, \cH_M = (\bm \mu \in \cO_M)$ where $\cO_1, \dots, \cO_M$ are open sets forming a partition of the set of possible means $\cO$. Our goal is to adaptively sample the arms until a decision is made that one of the hypotheses $\ihat$ is correct.

algorithms.name: Tracking rule (D-Tracking) with GLR stopping rule
GLR stopping rule with any sampling rule

source.label: prop:LB
source.quote: Define the complexity term $T^*(\bm \mu)$ as $T^*(\bm\mu)^{-1}= \sup_{\bm w \in \Sigma_K} \inf_{\bm \lambda \in \Alt(\bm\mu)} \sum_{a=1}^Kw_a d(\mu_a,\lambda_a)$ ... Then any $\delta$-correct strategy satisfies $\forall \bm\mu \in \cO, \ \bE_{\bm\mu}[\tau_{\delta}] \geq T^*(\bm\mu) \ln \left(\frac{1}{3\delta}\right)$.

results.notes: Generalises the Garivier-Kaufmann (2016) BAI lower bound using the same change-of-measure argument. T_star is the characteristic time of the general identification problem.

conditions: for every mu in O there is a unique vector of optimal weights w*(mu)
mu -> w*(mu) is continuous on each O_i
tuning: GLR stopping thresholds c_t(delta) deterministic, increasing in t, with c_t(delta) <= ln(D t/delta) for t >= C
forced exploration of arms with N_a(t) <= sqrt(t) - K/2

source.label: thm:OptimalTesting
source.quote: Assume that ... For every $\bm \mu \in \cO$, there is a unique vector of optimal weights ... the mapping $\bm \mu \mapsto \w^*(\bm \mu)$ is continuous on $\cO_i$. ... Let $\tau_\delta$ be the GLR stopping rule \eqref{eq:GLR.stop} with thresholds $\hat{c}_t(\delta)$. The Tracking rule \eqref{eq:tracking.rule} ensures \[\limsup_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\bE_{\bm\mu}\left[\tau_\delta\right]}{\ln(1/\delta)} = T^*(\bm\mu).\]

results.notes: This is an equality, so it matches the lower bound of Proposition 16. Combined with Proposition 15 it gives a delta-correct, asymptotically optimal test. The BAI threshold (eq. BetterThreshold) also satisfies the assumptions.

tuning: threshold c_t(delta) = 3 sum_a ln(1+ln N_a(t)) + K C_exp(ln(1/delta)/K)

source.label: prop:GLRAnalysis
source.quote: The sequence of thresholds $\hat{c}_t(\delta) = 3 \sum_{a = 1}^K \ln(1 + \ln N_a(t)) + K \cC_{\emph{exp}}\left(\frac{\ln(1/\delta)}{K}\right)$ is such that, \emph{for every sampling rule}, \[\bP_{\bm\mu}(\forall t \in \N, \bm \mu \in \cC_t(\delta)) \geq 1 - \delta \ \ \ \text{and} \ \ \ \bP_{\bm\mu}\left(\tau_\delta < \infty, \ihat(\tau_\delta) \neq i^*(\bm\mu)\right) \leq \delta.\]

results.notes: This is a delta-correctness guarantee (error probability <= delta), recorded as an error_probability bound.

tuning: threshold c_t(delta) = 3 R ln(1+ln(t/R)) + R C_exp(ln((M-1)/delta)/R)

source.label: prop:PACrank
source.quote: Fix an identification problem of rank $R$. Then the GLR stopping rule \eqref{eq:GLR} is $\delta$-correct with threshold \[ \hat c_t(\delta) ~=~ 3 R \ln (1+\ln(t/R)) + R \cC_{\text{exp}} \del*{\frac{\ln \frac{M-1}{\delta}}{R}} \]

results.notes: delta-correctness for any sampling rule. Special cases in the text: BAI (rank 2) and Largest Profit Identification (rank 4).
